evidence.quote: Also, although the labor market is robust, there is no evidence that rising wages are putting upward pressure on price inflation.
I myself believe that the range of plausible estimates of u* extends to 4 percent and below and includes the current unemployment rate of 3.7 percent.
Persistent inflation shortfalls carry the risk that longer-term inflation expectations become anchored below the stated inflation goal.
In many models that incorporate the ELB, these makeup strategies lead to better average performance on both legs of the dual mandate.
The unemployment rate is near a 50-year low, and inflation is running close to our 2 percent objective.
